topics.topic: Deterministic handling and port selection for multiple oversized mapped output lists
questions: Does the operation report all oversized lists, an unnamed over-ceiling result, or one deterministic first list; if one, what is its order?
When several delivered value-output lists exceed the ceiling, what result is returned, which list if any is named, and in what output-port order are lists built and checked?
When two or more delivered output lists exceed the ceiling, what exact failure result is returned, which port is named, and in what port order is that choice made?

judgement.why: This asks the same deterministic oversized-list selection and ordering question already judged in P1, and the later passages deciding it have not changed.

precedent.topic: Deterministic ordering and failure precedence when multiple mapped lists are assembled or oversized
quotes: assemble_mapped_lists: [BEHAVIOR] MUST build, for each MappedList in the order given, the list its elements' outputs make in element order, and write and publish nothing: a value list is one StoredValue whose bytes are canonical_bytes of the list of the elements' values — each read with read_value_bytes —, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) as items, of the class highest_disclosure_class gives for the elements' StoredValues — read through read_records with one RecordsById naming their value_ids —, its value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent; a file list is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements' SpooledFilesRefs.

assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.
precedent.why: The later notes require processing in the supplied order and select the first oversized port in that order after measuring all value lists.

topics.topic: Exact context and trace inputs required by plan_run
questions: What exact facts and record types constitute the run context, and which of them are distinct from the Run, pinned FlowVersion, ports and trace already listed?

What exactly is contained in “its context,” and what exact records and value references constitute “its trace,” including their required ordering and whether Run outputs and WaitingPoints are inputs or must be ignored and re-derived?
What exact facts constitute “its context,” which of those facts are distinct from the run, pinned version, ports and trace, and which records or values must `runs` pass?

quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity with when_missing unknown_reference, its pinned graph with read_flow_version and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, build its RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError, and then repeat, reading the trace again after every change: ask plan_run; when it derived drafts, write them in one RecordRunProgressChange; otherwise, when it names a next node, take that node's elements in the order given, as the next notes say; otherwise write the final change and stop. Every change goes through record_change with the given actor, and every time comes from kernel_now at the moment the field names.

read_records: [BEHAVIOR] Relation queries continue: ActivationBeforeRun the latest FlowActivation of the flow version whose store position is below the Run record's store position; ExecutionsOfRun the run's NodeExecutions together with the SpooledFiles they name; RunsByStatus the runs whose status is any of the given statuses — one list_run_rows_by_status per status, merged by store position without repeats — oldest first in store order; ApprovalsOfElement the element's EffectApprovals; AttemptsOfElement the element's EffectAttempts; AttemptsByStatus the effect attempts with that status; ActiveGrantOfNode the StandingGrant with status active for that flow version and node, or none.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] The ports a node's inputs and outputs are checked against MUST come from what the node names: a function node's from read_contract_version of its pinned implementation's contract version, an operation node's from read_binding of its binding_id; they are read once per advance and passed to plan_run as one NodePorts per flow node in node_id order.
judgement.why: The later notes enumerate RunContext, define the trace as ExecutionsOfRun, and specify the node-port inputs and their ordering.
judgement.failure: the deciding quote is not found verbatim in the later states' texts

topics.topic: Result and sandbox classification for an unreadable or malformed runner report
questions: What exact result is returned for an empty, truncated, malformed or multiply framed report, and how can sandbox distinguish it from a valid report whose returned outputs are not representable?
What exact result does `read_runner_report` return for an empty, truncated, malformed, multiply framed or otherwise unreadable report, and how must `sandbox` classify that result?
What result does `read_runner_report` return for an unreadable, truncated or otherwise malformed report so that `sandbox` can distinguish it from a valid report with no outputs?

judgement.why: This is the same malformed or incomplete runner-report result question already judged in P2, with unchanged deciding passages.

precedent.topic: Exact malformed or unreadable runner-report result
quotes: read_runner_report: [BEHAVIOR] The program writes each message as one line of UTF-8 JSON ended by a newline, an object whose kind is trap (with the trapped name), resource, crashed (with failure, the exception's type and message or null) or returned (with is_dict and outputs, each port, form, json_text and contents, the bytes base64-encoded). read_runner_report MUST decode the lines in order: trap names in the order written, resource_hit true when any resource line is present, crashed and failure from a crashed line, returned only from one complete returned line; a line that is not complete JSON of a known kind, the last line cut short included, ends the decoding and what follows is ignored.

read_runner_report: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns RunnerReport with trap_hits, resource_hit, crashed, failure and returned (None when no complete returned line was read), each ReturnedOutput's json_text set only for form json and contents holding the file's bytes, or the list's in order, only for file and file_list.
precedent.why: The later notes define malformed or partial input as terminating decoding and return a RunnerReport whose returned field is absent unless a complete returned line was read.

topics.topic: Timestamp ownership, timing, sharing, and determinism for derived drafts
questions: Which module obtains started_at and ended_at for these records, and at exactly what event: derivation by plan_run or the record_change that persists them?

Are `started_at` and `ended_at` the time `plan_run` derives the draft or a fresh time taken when `runs` actually performs `record_run_progress`, and is one reading shared by all drafts in that change or taken once per draft?
Does determinism exclude draft timestamps, or must timestamps be supplied or assigned outside `plan_run` so identical run facts produce an identical complete result?

Are `started_at` and `ended_at` the earlier time at which `plan_run` derives the draft, or must they be read when `runs` actually performs the store change; and is the reading shared by all drafts in that change or taken once per draft?
Is a draft's timestamp part of `plan_run`'s output even though that makes equal inputs produce different answers, or must `plan_run` return timeless drafts for `runs` to stamp when persisting them?

quotes:
Every timestamp an operation records comes from
  `clock.kernel_now`, taken at the moment the field names: a `started_at` when
  the execution or send begins — for an operation's NodeExecution, the
  `recorded_at` of its EffectAttempt when it has one (A11 rule 4) — every other
  time when its store change is made.

A `skipped_by_guard` or
  `upstream_failed` draft is stamped by `run_graph.plan_run` with one reading
  for both times, and `runs` writes it in its very next change, so that reading
  is the moment of its store change.
judgement.why: One passage requires these timestamps to be read when the store change is made, while the other requires plan_run to read them before runs performs that later change.

topics.topic: Publication and failure handling for mapped-list bytes recorded as a flow output
questions: Must record_flow_output publish the mapped list's canonical bytes before recording its StoredValue, and how are digest mismatch, publication refusal and I/O failure reported?

Does `record_flow_output` publish the mapped list's canonical bytes with `store.put_value_bytes` before `record_delivery_values`, and how are digest/size refusal or publication failure reported after any earlier publication?

quotes: A mapped node's value list that reaches a flow output is written as a StoredValue M21.
None of its own; a failed store change is `internal_error`.

`refused` when digest or size do not match; `internal_error` on a link or I/O
failure, nothing published.

record_flow_output: [BEHAVIOR] A RecordedSource MUST answer its ref; a MappedListSource MUST publish its list's StoredValue with put_value_bytes and write it in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange through record_change under the given actor before answering its ref; it checks nothing, since a flow output holds the value its edge delivered and is of value carriage (A05 rule 7).
judgement.divergence: One implementation propagates put_value_bytes' `refused` result for a digest or size mismatch, while another converts every publication failure to `internal_error`; runs and the MCP caller observe different error codes and retry behavior.
judgement.why: The later notes require publication before recording, but neither they nor the State 5 operation decide how its publication refusal is exposed or converted.

topics.topic: Runner report-channel and event-size bounds and the outcome when exceeded or left open
questions: What bounds reading of the report channel, what happens when it exceeds that bound or never closes, and which execution outcome results, given that the parent owns the wall deadline and output-count decision?
What bounds the report channel and the number or total bytes of trap events, exceptions and framing data, and what result is produced when that bound is exceeded?

quotes: Every byte the runner wrote to its channel, read by the parent until the channel closed.

The trap hits in the order they were written, whether a bound was hit inside, the type and message of an exception that escaped loading or `run`, and the outputs `run` returned, each as JSON text, a file, a file list or not representable.

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write into the exchange directory the runner_source text, the code, and every input — a value port's canonical JSON, a file port's bytes, a many file port one file per element in list order — and start the interpreter on the runner file with the runner_arguments of a RunnerLaunch naming those files by their paths inside the environment, the output ports, the bounds and the channel's descriptor number; it MUST close its own copy of the channel's write end once bubblewrap has started, read the channel while the environment runs until it closes, and decode what it read with read_runner_report. The parent sets no setrlimit limit: there the process limit would count every process of the user on the host and bubblewrap could not create its namespace (EAGAIN).

execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] The parent MUST enforce from outside a wall deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken when the environment starts plus bounds.wall_time_ms in nanoseconds and held in a local variable of execute_function only, after which — once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it — it kills every process of the environment by sending SIGKILL, through a pidfd, to the environment's PID-namespace init, the child-pid bubblewrap reports on --info-fd — not to bubblewrap itself or its process group — and then waits for bubblewrap to exit.
judgement.divergence: One implementation buffers an unlimited number of report bytes until the wall deadline or channel close, risking host-memory exhaustion, while another imposes a private byte or event ceiling and terminates or classifies the execution when it is crossed; the kernel process and the caller observe different availability and SandboxResult outcomes.
judgement.why: The wall deadline resolves a channel that remains open, but no text fixes a byte or event bound or the outcome when such a bound is exceeded.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Accepted source variants and persistence behavior of record_flow_output
questions: What closed source variants may be passed—an existing StoredValue, a flow input or constant, a function or operation output, or an unpersisted mapped-list result—and for each variant does the operation write `record_delivery_values` or simply return an existing reference?

topics.topic: Applicable size bounds for each deliver_input value or file form
questions: Which size bound is passed to `fit_port_value` for a delivered value, a file and a many-file reference, since `fit_port_value` requires the applicable bound but `deliver_input` does not name one?

topics.topic: Element conclusion after a not_applied resolution but before approval creation
questions: What conclusion does operation_element_conclusion return after an attempt is resolved not_applied but before request_approval has been written, including after a crash in that interval?

topics.topic: Executable elements returned for a partially concluded mapped node
questions: For a mapped node with succeeded, failed, waiting and not-yet-reached elements, exactly which elements does plan_run return for execution?

topics.topic: Inherited runner communication descriptors and their encoded descriptor numbers
questions: How many inherited writable descriptors exist, what is each one's role, and which descriptor numbers must `runner_arguments` receive and encode?

topics.topic: Ordering and replanning priority among drafts, flow outputs, delivery work, and executable nodes
questions: If one call returns newly determined drafts together with a ready node or newly produced flow outputs, which action must `runs` perform first, and must it re-run `plan_run` after recording drafts or outputs before executing the returned node?

topics.topic: Recovery behavior after an outcome_unknown attempt is resolved applied
questions: When an `outcome_unknown` attempt was resolved `applied`, does recovery accept the derived succeeded/failed conclusion without reaching the element, or call `reach_operation_element` again?

topics.topic: Representation and disclosure class of an empty mapped file-list reference
questions: What record/reference representation stores an empty file list and its required disclosure class, given that it contains no SpooledFile whose class can carry that fact and M23 defines no separate file-list reference?

topics.topic: Representation and persistence status of flow outputs produced by plan_run
questions: Does each produced flow output contain an already persisted StoredValue reference, an unpersisted mapped-list source for `run_values.record_flow_output`, or a closed union of both, and how does `runs` tell which outputs still require writing?

topics.topic: Responsibility for deterministic sandbox environment initialization
questions: Must `sandbox` launch the interpreter with only `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, must the runner clear and set the environment after interpreter startup, or must both do so?

Does the operation return an unpersisted StoredValue draft, a source object carrying canonical bytes plus prospective StoredValue facts, or only element references from which `deliver_input` must rebuild the value?

topics.topic: Runner input metadata and serialization or directory layout by carriage and cardinality
questions: What exact per-input metadata is passed to the runner, and what serialization or directory layout does each carriage/cardinality use?

topics.topic: Store effects and returned references when deliver_input receives non-derived sources
questions: For an already-written StoredValue, a single SpooledFile, or a mapped file-list reference, must `deliver_input` perform no store change and return the existing reference, or create some new delivery record; and what precisely is the returned ‘written reference’ for file inputs?
